title: Divisors, principal divisors, class group
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $C$ a smooth connected curve over $k$ ([def-sc-curves]). A *divisor* on $C$ is a finite formal sum $D=\sum_P n_P[P]$ of closed points with integer coefficients; $\operatorname{Div}(C)$ is the free abelian group on those points. For $f\in k(C)^*$ ([def-sc-function-field]), its *principal divisor* is $\operatorname{div}(f)=\sum_Pv_P(f)[P]$, where $v_P$ is the normalized valuation of $\mathcal O_{C,P}$. Its finite support follows from the finite-zero-and-pole theorem for rational functions. The local rings are discrete valuation rings by [lem-sc-smooth-regular] and [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr]. The *divisor class group* is $\operatorname{Cl}(C):=\operatorname{Div}(C)/\operatorname{im}(\operatorname{div})$. For a nonempty open $U\subseteq C$, the associated sub-$\mathcal O_C$-module of the constant sheaf $k(C)$ ([def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]) has sections $\mathcal O_C(D)(U):=\{0\}\cup\{f\in k(C)^*:v_P(f)+n_P\geq0\text{ for every closed }P\in U\}$; over the empty open its section module is zero. The assertion that $\mathcal O_C(D)$ is invertible and that $D\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(D)]$ identifies $\operatorname{Cl}(C)$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ is a separate theorem. The *degree* is $\deg D:=\sum_Pn_P$. For a disconnected smooth curve, these definitions apply componentwise.

proof.text: Construct the section submodule from the unchanged locally constant function predicate and closed-point order bounds. Zero satisfies the zero disjunct. For addition, separate a zero sum and zero summands. At coheight one, ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_coheight and [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] give the DVR instance; Scheme.ord_add bounds the sum by the minimum. At other coheights Scheme.ord_eq_zero_of_coheight_neq_one reduces the bound to that of a permitted nonzero summand.

For scalar closure, algebraMap_germ_eq_germToFunctionField identifies the scalar values at any two points of a nonempty integral open, making the scalar function constant. Multiply locally constant functions. Separate a zero scalar or zero section value; otherwise Scheme.ord_le_smul gives the required inequality. Introduce Nonempty U only after choosing a point, so the empty open is included and the pointwise scalar instance is unchanged.

Restriction is pointwise precomposition with the continuous open inclusion, retaining local constancy and the same closed-point bound. Its additivity, identity and composition are definitional equalities. Semilinearity follows pointwise from TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply. These proofs construct the semilinear restriction maps and module presheaf.

Realize the section condition as a TopCat.LocalPredicate. For locality, give the function field its discrete topology: local constancy is continuity by IsLocallyConstant.iff_continuous and continuity is local by TopCat.continuousLocal. Check each closed-point bound on a neighborhood containing that point. Apply TopCat.subpresheafToTypes.isSheaf and TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp' for the forgetful functor from abelian groups. The resulting associatedModule has the prescribed explicit sections, including the unique function on the empty open.

For moduleOfSmoothConnectedCurve, finite type supplies Noetherianity, IsConnectedCurve.connectedSpace' supplies connectedness, [lem-sc-smooth-regular] supplies IsRegular.of_smooth, and IsRegular.isIntegral supplies integrality. Apply the constructed associatedModule, without adding any hypothesis to the smooth connected curve interface.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $C$ be a connected curve over $k$. A
*divisor* on $C$ is a finite formal sum
$D=\sum_Pn_P[P]$ of closed points $P$ of $C$ with integer
coefficients; $\operatorname{Div}(C)$ is the free abelian group on
the closed points of $C$. For $f\in k(C)^*$
([def-sc-function-field]), its *divisor* is

$$
\operatorname{div}(f)=\sum_P v_P(f)\,[P],
$$

where $v_P$ is the normalized valuation of the local ring
$\mathcal O_{C,P}$ (a discrete valuation ring when $C$ is
smooth); such divisors are *principal*.
The *divisor class group* is

$$
\operatorname{Cl}(C):=\operatorname{Div}(C)/\{\operatorname{div}(f):f\in k(C)^*\}.
$$

For $D=\sum n_P[P]$ the associated sub-$\mathcal O_C$-module of
the constant sheaf $k(C)$ is

$$
\mathcal O_C(D)(U):=\{f\in k(C):\operatorname{div}(f)|_U+D|_U\geq0\}.
$$

The *degree* of $D$ is

$$
\deg D:=\sum_Pn_P.
$$

(For reducible $C$ all objects above are defined componentwise.)

For $C$ smooth, $\mathcal O_C(D)$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module,
and $D\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(D)]$ identifies $\operatorname{Cl}(C)$ with
$\operatorname{Pic}(C)$.
